items.reason: The 1996 general interpolation proof was not obtained, and no faithful open source-level description of its actual proof was obtained. It is therefore unresolved whether its proof contains a repair that transfers to total domination.
items.comparison: The 1999 preliminary proofs establish existence of valid orientations via strong orientations of cyclic blocks (pp. 161-162), a lower bound (pp. 162-163), and the extremal cycle characterization using Hall representatives and cycle-cover reductions (pp. 163-164). They contain no comparison of two arbitrary valid orientations, no target-directed safe flip and no blocked-flip transfer lemma. This does not establish the content of the unobtained 1996 proof. VanderJagt’s actual WMU dissertation is Local Connectivity in Graphs (April 1973); its open-access landing record was obtained but PDF access returned 403. Hansen’s author page instead identifies a 1997 thesis Domination in Digraphs, a potentially relevant distinct source, not obtained.
items.missing: An open copy of pp. 51-63 of the 1996 paper, or a reliable later primary treatment reproducing its interpolation proof, including allowed reversals and treatment of infeasible orientations.

items.reason: Publication is confirmed, but no newly obtained allowed primary text establishes retention of Conjecture 3.1 as open in the published version. Indexed publisher excerpts are suggestive and not promoted to a primary-body check.
items.comparison: Johnston’s research entry 20 links to the final publisher article, not a locally hosted accepted manuscript. The St. Thomas HTTP response is only an application shell. Search-indexed St. Thomas text confirms volume 382, pp. 48-59, 31 March 2026, but its abstract does not discuss interpolation. OpenAlex labels the publisher version closed and the arXiv location submittedVersion. Neither establishes the final conjecture’s open status. No request was sent to ScienceDirect.
items.missing: A legitimately accessible final or accepted body, or an allowed author/repository statement explicitly identifying the conjecture as retained and unresolved in that version.

items.reason: The bounded search was executed and found no new general resolving proof, but no complete citing-work list was obtained. The second and final permitted OpenAlex request returned 429; two new potential leads remained without primary bodies after access denials.
items.comparison: The first OpenAlex search returned 10 relevance-ranked works, not citing works. The modern paper is W4416573736 with cited_by_count 0; that index value is not proof of no citations (the already reviewed Blazsik-Nagy paper cites the preprint). The results include a June 2026 applications review, DOI 10.9734/jamcs/2026/v41i62159, whose primary publisher page returned 403. Exact-title, arXiv-ID and interpolation searches, including MathOverflow, yielded no newly identified general proof. The recent arXiv math.CO listing covers 464 entries across 28 October-4 November 2026; keyword screening found no orientable-domination or interpolation/reconfiguration lead. It includes an unrelated planar-triangulation total-domination title, not a claimed orientation-interpolation result. The complete multipartite paper remains a potentially relevant older citing work: indexed text identifies Theorem 3 as restricted to complete r-partite graphs and displays graph-specific orientation constructions; no primary PDF/body was obtained, so this is not source-level clearance.
items.missing: An accessible citing-work route with primary bodies for potentially relevant items, especially the Lai-Chiang-Lin-Yu paper if its proof machinery is to be ruled out. No exhaustive citation graph or worldwide priority search is claimed.
